Only verbatim CVE-YYYY-NNNN strings are valid for this category.
- Weakness: an explicit CWE identifier (e.g., CWE-89) or a core flaw mechanism.
- Configuration: a specific product, software, component, device, or CPE identifier that could be affected by vulnerabilities. Extract each distinct ID occurrence as its own entity using solely the exact ID substring (e.g., from "Valid Accounts (T1078, ICS T0859)" extract "T1078" and "T0859" separately, not the full phrase; the "ICS " prefix MUST be dropped and only the T-code "T0859" is taken). Sub-technique IDs (e.g., T1090.002) and parent technique IDs (e.g., T1090) are both valid when explicitly present. CRITICAL: MITRE ATT&CK TACTIC IDs formatted as TAxxxx (e.g., TA0009, TA0010, TA0011) are OUT OF SCOPE and MUST NOT be extracted as AttackTechnique or any other type. ICS-prefixed technique mentions (e.g., "ICS T0859") ARE IN SCOPE: extract only the exact T-code token (e.g., "T0859") and discard the "ICS " prefix.

PARENT TECHNIQUE DERIVATION RULE (MANDATORY):
When you extract a sub-technique ID of the form Txxxx.yyy (e.g., T1036.004, T1090.002, T1574.014) as an AttackTechnique entity from the text, you MUST ALSO emit the corresponding parent technique ID (Txxxx, e.g., T1036, T1090, T1574) as a DISTINCT separate AttackTechnique entity, UNLESS the parent ID already appears elsewhere in the input text as its own verbatim span (in which case only extract that verbatim span, do not synthesize).   - "start" MUST equal the start offset of the extracted sub-technique ID substring in the input.
  - "end" MUST equal start + length of the parent ID (i.e., 5 for Txxxx, pointing to the character just after the parent portion, before the dot).
  - "normalized_id" MUST be the parent ID (e.g., "T1036").
